proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Fit rotation curves and cluster lensing masses with one global parameter set; failure if the enclosed-mass gating forces opposite-sign amplitudes for the two classes.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Galaxies follow a tight radial-acceleration relation while clusters receive extra boost at large radii where the enclosed-mass kernel remains high.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Kernel saturation could make the product nearly constant, collapsing the structure to a plain rescaled MOND law.
proposals.mechanism: A bounded log-acceleration permittivity provides the universal low-acceleration boost, but it is multiplied against an interior-integral kernel of enclosed baryonic mass so that the response depends on how mass is distributed inside the radius rather than only on the local acceleration. This preserves a single acceleration scale while allowing clusters (broad mass kernels) and disks (compact kernels) to differ.
source_domains: dielectric analogy in nonlinear Poisson equations
proposals.title: Acceleration-scale permittivity gated by enclosed-mass kernel
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Standard MOND permittivity is strictly local in acceleration; multiplying by a nonlocal enclosed-mass kernel introduces distribution dependence that cannot be absorbed into a redefinition of the interpolating function.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Compare boost amplitudes for isolated vs group galaxies at matched baryonic acceleration; falsified if no environmental ordering appears.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Isolated galaxies show larger boosts than equally luminous cluster members; cluster lensing profiles steepen relative to isolated systems.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Normalized contrast may be degenerate with radius, mimicking a pure radial law with no true environment sensitivity.
proposals.mechanism: The response is set by the contrast between a compact internal geometry-density product and an exterior nonlocal outer-potential kernel. Where the internal term dominates (galaxy inner disks) response is suppressed; where the external potential dominates (cluster outskirts, group environments) response rises, encoding an external field effect through explicit nonlocal weighting.
proposals.title: Geometry-density contrast against outer potential memory
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: The external field effect is usually a boundary condition on the field equation; here it enters as an explicit normalized contrast coordinate, giving a different functional dependence than any local mu-function rewrite.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Test whether required boost correlates with axis ratio at fixed acceleration; falsified if the anisotropy term needs zero weight.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Thin disks and spheroids of identical baryonic acceleration exhibit measurably different dynamical-to-baryonic mass ratios.
known_analogues: Anisotropic lensing shear response in TeVeS-like models
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Anisotropy proxies may be too noisy or too weakly varying to break degeneracy with amplitude.
proposals.mechanism: A screened auxiliary field driven by the bounded logarithmic mass slope sets how strongly the medium responds to the transition from mass-dominated to vacuum-dominated regions; this is gated by a shape-anisotropy tensor scalar so that flattened disks and near-spherical clusters receive geometrically distinct amplitudes from a single law.
proposals.title: Mass-slope screening times shape anisotropy
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Combining a slope-driven screened auxiliary with an explicit anisotropy gate produces shape-dependent gravity that no isotropic acceleration-based rewrite reproduces.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Check whether required amplitude at fixed baryonic acceleration is independent of physical radius; falsified if no radius trend exists.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Boost grows with physical radius even at fixed acceleration, giving clusters extra lensing amplitude at Mpc scales.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Radius coordinate may overshoot in cluster outskirts, producing unphysically large lensing convergence.
proposals.mechanism: A bi-Helmholtz auxiliary field on bounded log acceleration supplies two smoothing lengths, capturing both galactic-scale and cluster-scale filtering. This is additively combined with the dimensionless cosmological group R*H/c so that the transition radius inherits a Hubble-scale reference, tying the acceleration scale to expansion rather than positing it independently.

proposals.title: Bi-Helmholtz two-scale response with cosmic clock coordinate
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Two-scale nonlocal filtering plus an explicit Hubble-length coordinate yields scale-dependent behavior between galaxies and clusters that a single-scale nonlocal kernel cannot mimic.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Split clusters into relaxed and disturbed samples; falsified if inferred boost is identical within errors.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Dynamically disturbed or merging systems show weaker boosts than relaxed systems of the same baryonic profile.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Memory proxies may be effectively constant per object, degenerating into a per-object nuisance offset.
proposals.mechanism: Gravity response tracks a causal-history memory of the mass log slope, representing accumulated assembly of the baryonic distribution, but is limited by the instantaneous mass log curvature via a weighted minimum so that sharply curved, recently reconfigured regions cannot inherit full historical response. This encodes causal lag in the gravitational medium.
proposals.title: Causal memory of mass slope minimized against local curvature
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: A weighted minimum between a memory coordinate and an instantaneous curvature coordinate is a non-smooth regime selector, not obtainable by reparameterizing a single-argument response function.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Compare outer rotation curves of sharply truncated versus extended HI disks at matched acceleration.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Truncated baryon distributions (steeply falling outer profiles) show suppressed boost at large radii relative to extended ones.
known_analogues: Two-sided Green's function decomposition of Poisson solutions
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Sign cancellations in the geometric mean may drive the response toward the neutral midpoint over most of the data.
proposals.mechanism: The Poisson solution splits into interior and exterior contributions; here the response is the signed geometric mean of an interior acceleration-contrast kernel and an exterior acceleration-contrast kernel, so the boost is large only when both inner and outer mass arrangements jointly support it. This enforces a multiplicative consistency between local dynamics and outer lensing reach.
proposals.title: Signed geometric mean of interior and exterior acceleration contrasts
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Geometric-mean coupling of two oppositely oriented nonlocal kernels is not equivalent to any weighted sum or single local function of acceleration.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Locate onset radius in units of Rb across surface-brightness bins; falsified if onset is fixed in acceleration but not in R/Rb.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Boost onset occurs at a nearly fixed number of baryonic scale lengths, giving low-surface-brightness galaxies earlier onset in acceleration units.
known_analogues: p-Laplacian / adaptive gradient nonlinear Poisson models
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Cluster Rb definitions may be ill-posed, breaking universality between the two data classes.
proposals.mechanism: An adaptive-gradient auxiliary field responds to the local steepness of the geometry-density product, sharpening the response where baryons transition rapidly. Its difference from the dimensionless radius-to-baryon-scale ratio R/Rb makes the effective transition occur at a fixed multiple of the baryonic scale length, giving an internally set rather than universally fixed transition.

proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Making the transition track each system's own baryonic scale radius rather than a fixed acceleration produces predictions that differ systematically across surface-brightness classes.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Search for a crossover feature in stacked lensing profiles; falsified if profiles are smooth with no regime switch at any consistent location.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Two distinct boost regimes with a fairly abrupt crossover in radius, visible as a kink in cluster lensing mass profiles.

proposals.likely_failure_mode: One channel may dominate everywhere, rendering the second term and its switching surface unidentifiable.
proposals.mechanism: A mixed two-field auxiliary driven by bounded mass slope provides a moderate baseline response; a weighted maximum with an exterior outer-slope-contrast kernel lets whichever channel is stronger set the boost. Physically the medium has two excitation channels, a locally sourced one and an outer-boundary-sourced one, and the dominant channel governs the response.
proposals.title: Mixed two-field permittivity maximized with outer slope contrast
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Channel-dominance via a weighted maximum creates a piecewise regime structure with a switching surface that smooth additive rewrites cannot reproduce.

proposals.mechanism: A bounded log-acceleration permittivity coordinate sets the baseline boost, and an interior-integral enclosed-mass kernel multiplicatively gates it so that the response only saturates where the mass reservoir interior to the radius is already large; this couples local acceleration to a nonlocal source measure rather than to radius alone.

proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Standard interpolating functions depend only on local acceleration; multiplying by a kernel-weighted enclosed-mass coordinate makes the boost explicitly nonlocal, which cannot be absorbed into a redefinition of the local interpolating function.

proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: It is not a function of acceleration or radius but of the mismatch between two oppositely oriented nonlocal kernels, so it cannot be rewritten as any single-scale interpolating law.

proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Combining a time-history floor with a geometry-conditioned memory gate makes the boost depend on assembly history and shape jointly, which no purely instantaneous acceleration law reproduces.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Test inner rotation curves of bulge-dominated spirals; if the predicted suppression is absent in data, reject.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Smooth extended halos in clusters with suppressed response near sharp baryonic concentrations such as BCG cores and galaxy bulges.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Curvature estimates from noisy photometric profiles could produce spurious oscillatory suppression.
proposals.mechanism: A two-scale bi-Helmholtz auxiliary field driven by bounded log-acceleration supplies a smoothed long-range response; it is combined by weighted difference against a local mass-log-curvature coordinate, so regions of sharp profile curvature partially cancel the smoothed field, mimicking reflection at an impedance mismatch.
proposals.title: Optical impedance mismatch: bi-Helmholtz auxiliary field against a local curvature scale
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: The subtraction of a local curvature term from a two-scale nonlocal field introduces a genuine cancellation channel absent from single-kernel nonlocal gravity formulations.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Stack lensing profiles split by cluster ellipticity at fixed mass; absence of the predicted split falsifies.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Boost correlates with measured ellipticity/flattening and with mass lying beyond the probe radius, predicting stronger lensing in elongated cluster configurations.

proposals.likely_failure_mode: Projected anisotropy is orientation-dependent, so the intrinsic signal may be washed out and the term degenerate to a constant.
proposals.mechanism: Couple a shape-anisotropy times geometry tensor coordinate to an exterior nonlocal outer-potential kernel through a signed geometric mean, so that the boost requires both an anisotropic local configuration and a substantial mass exterior to the radius; either alone gives a modest response.
proposals.title: Signed geometric mean of a shape-anisotropy tensor coordinate and an exterior potential kernel
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: A multiplicative geometric-mean AND-gate between anisotropy and exterior potential is not reducible to an additive external-field correction nor to an isotropic interpolating function.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Search for the predicted kink where the max switches branches in high-quality rotation curves; smooth data with no branch behaviour disfavours it.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Flat outer rotation curves with a floored, weakly radius-dependent boost, plus enhanced cluster lensing where acceleration profiles steepen.
known_analogues: Automatic gain control in signal processing
proposals.likely_failure_mode: The max may lock onto one branch for nearly all data, collapsing the structure to a single-primitive law.
proposals.mechanism: An adaptive-gradient auxiliary field on bounded log-acceleration supplies a self-limiting boost whose gain shrinks where gradients are steep; a weighted maximum with the local acceleration log-slope ensures the response never drops below a slope-driven floor, giving a saturating-but-floored gain profile.
proposals.title: Adaptive-gain auxiliary field limited by a soft maximum against acceleration slope
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: The max operator introduces a non-smooth switch between two distinct physical channels (adaptive gain and slope floor) that no single smooth interpolating function encodes.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Compare required boosts for isolated versus group-embedded galaxies at matched baryonic profile; no environmental dependence falsifies.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Boost amplitude depends on large-scale environment at fixed internal dynamics; isolated galaxies and cluster cores differ systematically.
known_analogues: Dimensionless pi-group scaling in fluid dynamics
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Environment proxies may be poorly constrained observationally, so the threshold term becomes unconstrained and effectively free.
proposals.mechanism: An environment-times-field pair-product coordinate acts as a connectivity order parameter for the response, and it is combined by weighted difference with a dimensionless radius-to-cosmic-acceleration pi group so that the boost turns on only when environmental connectivity exceeds the local scale demand, echoing a percolation threshold.
proposals.title: Network percolation analogue: environment-field pair product contrasted with radial pi-group scale
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Threshold competition between an environmental connectivity coordinate and an explicit dimensionless cosmological pi group is a cross-domain construction, not a reparameterization of an acceleration-only law.

proposals.idea_07: {"proposal_id":"idea_07","title":"Adaptive-gain auxiliary field limited by a soft maximum against acceleration slope","origin_self_assessment":"known_family_combination","known_analogues":["Automatic gain control in signal processing","Adaptive-gradient (p-Laplacian-like) nonlinear field equations","QUMOND-type auxiliary field solutions"],"source_domains":["control theory gain limiting","nonlinear PDE field theory","cluster gas dynamics"],"mechanism":"An adaptive-gradient auxiliary field on bounded log-acceleration supplies a self-limiting boost whose gain shrinks where gradients are steep; a weighted maximum with the local acceleration log-slope ensures the response never drops below a slope-driven floor, giving a saturating-but-floored gain profile.","left_primitive_id":426,"left_transform":"identity","right_primitive_id":270,"right_transform":"absolute","binary_operator":"weighted_max","mixing":0.75,"suggested_amplitude":3.0,"suggested_acceleration_exponent":0.2,"suggested_transition_u":2.0,"why_not_merely_a_rewrite":"The max operator introduces a non-smooth switch between two distinct physical channels (adaptive gain and slope floor) that no single smooth interpolating function encodes.","expected_observational_signature":"Flat outer rotation curves with a floored, weakly radius-dependent boost, plus enhanced cluster lensing where acceleration profiles steepen.","cheapest_falsifier":"Search for the predicted kink where the max switches branches in high-quality rotation curves; smooth data with no branch behaviour disfavours it.","likely_failure_mode":"The max may lock onto one branch for nearly all data, collapsing the structure to a single-primitive law."}
proposals.idea_08: {"proposal_id":"idea_08","title":"Network percolation analogue: environment-field pair product contrasted with radial pi-group scale","origin_self_assessment":"uncertain","known_analogues":["Percolation thresholds in random networks","Environment-dependent screening in symmetron models","Dimensionless pi-group scaling in fluid dynamics"],"source_domains":["network percolation","screened scalar field cosmology","dimensional analysis"],"mechanism":"An environment-times-field pair-product coordinate acts as a connectivity order parameter for the response, and it is combined by weighted difference with a dimensionless radius-to-cosmic-acceleration pi group so that the boost turns on only when environmental connectivity exceeds the local scale demand, echoing a percolation threshold.","left_primitive_id":14,"left_transform":"tanh_2x","right_primitive_id":102,"right_transform":"signed_square_root","binary_operator":"weighted_difference","mixing":-0.5,"suggested_amplitude":0.6,"suggested_acceleration_exponent":0.35,"suggested_transition_u":0.5,"why_not_merely_a_rewrite":"Threshold competition between an environmental connectivity coordinate and an explicit dimensionless cosmological pi group is a cross-domain construction, not a reparameterization of an acceleration-only law.","expected_observational_signature":"Boost amplitude depends on large-scale environment at fixed internal dynamics; isolated galaxies and cluster cores differ systematically.","cheapest_falsifier":"Compare required boosts for isolated versus group-embedded galaxies at matched baryonic profile; no environmental dependence falsifies.","likely_failure_mode":"Environment proxies may be poorly constrained observationally, so the threshold term becomes unconstrained and effectively free."}

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Test whether asymmetry in gradient sign correlates with residual scatter; absence of asymmetry falsifies the signed-square treatment.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Absence of a bump/plateau feature at intermediate densities in stacked lensing profiles would falsify the double-gate structure.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: No correlation between cluster dynamical age proxies and response residuals would falsify the time-dependence claim.

proposals.title: Triple geometric closure multiplied by exterior nonlocal outer-mass kernel
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Multiplying a three-field geometric closure by a nonlocal exterior-mass kernel introduces a coupling between local internal structure and mass integrated well beyond the local radius, a nonlocal amplification absent from local pair or triple products alone; this is structurally distinct from any single primitive.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Compare relaxed versus recently disturbed clusters/galaxies at matched current acceleration; absence of systematic offset falsifies memory-dependence.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Systems with recent dynamical disturbance (mergers, infall) show gravitational response lagging behind their current instantaneous acceleration state, detectable as offset residuals correlated with dynamical youth.
known_analogues: viscoelastic memory kernels in condensed matter
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Memory kernel parameters may be degenerate with baryonic feedback history, making the signal unresolvable from astrophysical confounds.
proposals.mechanism: tensor_scalar+causal_history
proposals.title: Additive blend of anisotropy-mass-slope tensor scalar and memory-weighted log-acceleration history
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Adding a tensorial anisotropy-mass-slope coupling to a causal memory-weighted log-acceleration term introduces path-dependence (hysteresis) into an otherwise instantaneous response function, a qualitatively different temporal structure than any static combination of the two primitives.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Search for a kink feature at the predicted transition_u in stacked acceleration relations; a smooth continuous transition without kink falsifies the max-dominance structure.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: A sharp regime boundary in the mass-discrepancy relation where one screening mechanism dominates at small radius and the other at large radius, producing a kink rather than a smooth transition.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Real transitions may be smoother than a hard max operator predicts, causing systematic mismatch near the crossover scale.
proposals.mechanism: source_conditioned_permittivity+bihelmholtz_auxiliary
proposals.title: Max-combination of tanh-bounded acceleration permittivity and dual-scale geometry auxiliary field
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Taking the elementwise maximum of an optics-inspired permittivity-style saturation and a dual-scale screened auxiliary field creates a piecewise-dominant regime switching behavior not achievable by any smooth additive or multiplicative combination of the two mechanisms.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Test galaxies matched in normalized mass-slope-to-gradient ratio but differing by an order of magnitude in absolute density; large discrepancy in predicted response falsifies the normalization assumption.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Response strength depends on the relative steepness of mass profile versus density gradient rather than their absolute values, predicting similar dynamical anomalies for galaxies of very different absolute density but similar profile shape.
known_analogues: adaptive gain control in feedback systems
normalized difference indices in remote sensing
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Ratio-based normalization can become numerically unstable or ill-defined in low-signal regions such as cluster outskirts, degrading predictive power there.
proposals.mechanism: convex_nonlinear_auxiliary+adaptive_gradient_auxiliary
proposals.title: Normalized contrast between convex nonlinear mass-slope auxiliary and adaptive gradient-density auxiliary
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: The normalized-contrast operator applied to a convex nonlinear auxiliary field and a sign-flipped adaptive gradient auxiliary produces a bounded ratio-like response sensitive to relative rather than absolute magnitudes of mass-slope and density-gradient structure, a form not reducible to either auxiliary field's native scaling.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Map the crossover radius predicted by the min-gate against observed rotation curve turnover radii across a mass range; systematic mismatch falsifies the min-dominance hypothesis.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: In the inner regions where enclosed mass is small, response tracks the enclosed-mass kernel; in outer regions the mixed geometry field takes over, producing a distinct crossover radius independent of the smooth interpolation forms typically assumed.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Hard minimum operator may produce unphysical discontinuities in force derivatives at the crossover, inconsistent with smooth observed rotation curves.
proposals.mechanism: mixed_two_field+interior_integral
proposals.title: Min-gated combination of dual-scale mixed geometry field and interior enclosed-mass kernel
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Taking the minimum of a dual-scale mixed geometry field and an interior enclosed-mass kernel enforces a hard bottleneck where whichever mechanism predicts the weaker response dominates, structurally different from additive or multiplicative blends and analogous to limiter behavior in circuits rather than any known gravity interpolation form.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Fit dwarf galaxy rotation curves; if the geometry gate forces mass-dependent a0 inconsistent with the BTFR, reject.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Flat rotation curves in galaxies plus a residual lensing boost in cluster cores where geometry*density is high.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Cluster lensing under-predicted because acceleration gate saturates before central overdensity contributes.
proposals.mechanism: A bounded acceleration ratio a0/(cH) sets the deep-field permittivity while a geometry*density product modulates the transition, giving a universal response usable at both galaxy and cluster scales.
proposals.title: Acceleration-scale permittivity gated by baryonic geometry
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: The acceleration scale is gated by an explicit baryonic geometry-density coordinate rather than by acceleration alone, breaking pure MOND functional form.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Compare predicted vs observed rotation velocity break radius against Rb in disk galaxies.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Rotation curve shape tracks cumulative enclosed baryons with a radial break near Rb, and lensing convergence follows enclosed-mass profile.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Nonlocal kernel over-smooths sharp bulge-dominated inner regions.
proposals.mechanism: An interior integral over enclosed mass provides a nonlocal source term, contrasted against local R/Rb radial position to build a scale-bridging response.
proposals.title: Enclosed-mass memory kernel with radial contrast
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Combines a genuine interior integral operator with a local radial ratio in a normalized contrast, not reducible to a single-variable interpolation.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Check whether rotation-supported and pressure-supported galaxies at same a lie on same effective response; if identical, anisotropy term is unneeded.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Divergent response amplitude between rotation-supported and dispersion-supported systems at fixed acceleration.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Anisotropy proxy poorly constrained observationally, degenerate with mass-slope.
proposals.mechanism: A tensor-scalar contraction of orbital anisotropy with the mass log-slope conditions the response, capturing how velocity structure differs between disks and pressure-supported clusters.
proposals.title: Anisotropy-conditioned mass-slope response
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Introduces an anisotropy tensor scalar as an explicit conditioning variable, which no scalar-only interpolation captures.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Look for absence of predicted outskirt boost in isolated low-density galaxies.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Suppressed modification in high-density cluster cores, enhanced in low-density galaxy outskirts and voids.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Screening too aggressive, killing needed cluster lensing enhancement.
proposals.mechanism: A screened auxiliary field sourced by geometry*density suppresses modification in dense baryonic cores while activating in diffuse outskirts, contrasted with a triple-closure environment term.
proposals.title: Screened auxiliary field from geometry-density product
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Couples a density-screened auxiliary field to an environment-conditioned triple closure, producing environment-dependent screening not present in single-field screening.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Compare high-z vs low-z lensing masses at fixed baryon content; no evolution falsifies memory term.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Redshift-dependent response amplitude; early-assembled systems show different effective mass discrepancy.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Degenerate with standard structure growth; hard to isolate memory signal.
proposals.mechanism: A causal history memory term weighted by local acceleration log-slope encodes retardation from the object's assembly history, linked to a Hubble-time coordinate H*t.
proposals.title: Cosmic-time causal memory times acceleration slope
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Adds an explicit causal-memory dependence on assembly history rather than an instantaneous state function.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Test whether response break correlates with density inflection radius in well-resolved galaxies.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Response breaks localized to profile inflection radii, distinct in cored vs cuspy systems.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Curvature proxies noisy, sensitive to profile fitting choices.
proposals.mechanism: A radial Laplacian proxy of the potential gates the response, contrasted with mass log-curvature, so transitions occur where the baryonic density profile inflects.
proposals.title: Radial-Laplacian curvature gate with mass slope
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Uses second-derivative curvature information of the baryon distribution as the trigger, distinct from acceleration-magnitude interpolations.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Compare isolated vs cluster-embedded dwarfs at fixed internal acceleration for EFE-like differences.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Internal dynamics of satellites depend on host environment; cluster galaxies show suppressed internal modification.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Weighted-max operator produces discontinuous switching between internal and external regimes.
proposals.mechanism: An exterior nonlocal kernel of outer mass couples to a bounded acceleration ratio Rb*a0/c^2, encoding an external-field-like influence on the internal response.
proposals.title: Exterior nonlocal mass with acceleration-scale ratio
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: Encodes an explicit exterior nonlocal source combined via weighted max with an acceleration scale, producing external-field dependence rather than a local law.

proposals.cheapest_falsifier: Check whether flattened vs round systems at same acceleration show the predicted amplitude offset.
proposals.expected_observational_signature: Smooth monotone response with amplitude modulated by system shape/flattening at both galaxy and cluster scales.
proposals.likely_failure_mode: Signed geometric mean unstable near zero-crossings of the anisotropy coordinate.
proposals.mechanism: A convex nonlinear auxiliary field of bounded log-acceleration is blended by signed geometric mean with a shape-anisotropy local term to keep the response monotone yet geometry-aware.
proposals.title: Convex auxiliary field from bounded log-acceleration
proposals.why_not_merely_a_rewrite: The convex auxiliary field is coupled through a signed geometric mean with a shape coordinate, enforcing joint monotone-geometric behavior absent in scalar interpolations.
